idea-plugin.name: ML Experiment Cockpit
idea-plugin.description:
Tools for machine learning and data science in your IDE: MLflow experiment tracking, Weights & Biases (wandb) sweeps, Optuna studies, the Model Registry — runs and metrics in PyCharm, IntelliJ, WebStorm, GoLand or CLion.

  • Experiments — your MLflow experiments and runs in a tree, with parameters, metric values and the full history of any metric as a curve.
  • Optuna — studies and trials from your Optuna Dashboard: summary, the five best trials and a bar chart of the hyperparameter that takes the most distinct values.
  • Models — the MLflow Model Registry: registered models, their versions, stage, status and run id.
  • Sweeps — W&B hyperparameter sweeps grouped by state, with their run count and timestamps (the W&B API does not expose a best run for a sweep).

All five tabs (Experiments, Optuna, Models, Sweeps and the Compare view) live in one ML Experiment Cockpit tool window, in PyCharm, IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, GoLand and CLion — any IntelliJ-platform IDE from build 243 to 263. This plugin is read-only: it reads your servers and never writes to them.

You see exactly what your server answers, within its own query limits: up to 500 experiments, 100 runs per experiment, 500 registered models, 500 model versions and 5 000 metric points per run; W&B sweeps are read without pagination (the first 50 sweeps).

ML Experiment Cockpit Pro adds exactly one tab — Compare: right-click a run in the Experiments tree, pick « Compare with… », and the two runs are shown side by side — parameters, last metric values with absolute and relative gaps — and both metric curves are drawn on the same axis, exportable as Markdown. Without a licence the tab stays visible but locked, and the four free tabs are unchanged.

It is a read-only MLOps view: experiment tracking, hyperparameter sweeps and registered models, read from the servers you configure. Open it from View | Tool Windows | ML Experiment Cockpit and set your servers in Settings | Tools | ML Experiment Cockpit. Every request goes to the servers you configure — no telemetry, no analytics, no advertising.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.1.9 - Pro: compare 2 runs and export the comparison as one standalone HTML file - the Pro trial is free for 30 days.

  • Pro only: compare 2 runs and export the comparison as one self-contained HTML file - and the Pro trial is free for 30 days.
  • The exported file carries the parameters, the latest metric values with the absolute and the relative gaps, and the curve of the metric. The style is integrated and the curve is an embedded image: the file opens offline, loads nothing from the network, and can be sent to someone who has no MLflow.
  • The trial is started from the plugin itself: click Start 30-day free trial in the Compare tab, then Evaluate for free in the JetBrains window (or Help | Register). The plugin never takes a payment: the Pro tier is sold at 29 EUR/year, VAT depending on your country, and the Marketplace page carries the price and the details.
  • Nothing else changes: the four free tabs, their limits, the comparison itself and the Markdown copy are unchanged.

2026.1.8 - The comparison can be shared as one standalone HTML file.

  • Pro only: a new Export button writes the comparison - parameters, latest metric values with the absolute and the relative gaps, and the curve of the metric - as one self-contained HTML file, that can be sent to someone who has no MLflow.
  • The report is self-contained: the style is integrated in the file and the curve is an embedded image. It opens offline and loads nothing from the network.
  • The file is written in the folder you choose, under the name ml-experiment-compare-<run A>-<run B>-<date>.html. The 2 runs are read again at that moment: if one of them has disappeared or has been renamed since the comparison, nothing is written and the tab says why.
  • Nothing else changes: the four free tabs, their limits, the comparison itself and the Markdown copy are unchanged.

2026.1.7 - The locked Compare tab now sells the Pro tier.

  • The locked tab says Compare is a Pro feature, states the price (29 EUR/year, VAT depending on your country) and the 30-day free trial, and links to the plugin page on the JetBrains Marketplace (price and details). The trial itself is started in the IDE.

2026.1.6 - The Pro tier price is now written in euros.

  • Every text of the plugin that names the price of the Pro tier — the description table, the locked Compare tab and these notes — now reads 29 EUR/year, VAT depending on your country. The Marketplace purchase dialog remains the one that shows the final price and takes the payment.
  • The Compare tab now says Pro: active when the Pro features are usable, without distinguishing a free trial from a paid licence.
  • No functional change: the four free tabs and the comparison itself are unchanged.

2026.1.5 - A mistyped server address now gives a clear message.

  • When the address of the MLflow or Optuna server is typed without its scheme (for example localhost:5000 instead of http://localhost:5000), the tab now reports Invalid MLflow URL: "localhost:5000" - the scheme is missing (http:// or https://) (or Invalid Optuna URL) instead of Unexpected error and a red error balloon.
  • No visible change when the address is correct: the same data, the same messages.

2026.1.4 - The licence check now verifies the JetBrains signature (official sample).

  • The Pro tier is now unlocked only by a licence stamp whose JetBrains signature is verified against the two public JetBrains root certificates, with the official JetBrains sample. A hand-written stamp no longer opens the paid tab.
  • No visible change for a customer with a valid licence or during the free trial.

2026.1.3 - The purchase dialog is opened with the current platform APIs.

  • The "Get Pro" button now opens the JetBrains purchase dialog through the platform's current action API: the plugin reports no deprecated, removed or override-only API usage on recent IDE versions.
  • No visible change: the same dialog, the same product code and the same message.

2026.1.2 - The Compare tab is unlocked as soon as the licence becomes active.

  • The licence state is read again when the purchase dialog closes, so the Compare tab opens instead of staying locked.

2026.1.1 - Compare tab: the real price, the licence read again, and the platform's pooled threads.

  • The locked Compare tab now displays the Pro tier price (29 EUR/year, VAT depending on your country) and mentions the free trial without promising a duration (the trial length is the one configured in the Marketplace sale settings).
  • The licence state is read again every time the Compare tab becomes visible again (for instance when the IDE had just started and the licence could not be read yet), so the tab is not left locked for a customer who has a licence.
  • The status line is now shown under both views of the tab, so a purchase dialog that cannot be opened is reported instead of failing silently.
  • If the second run is changed while the comparison is being computed, the comparison is computed again for the new run instead of showing the previous one.
  • A late answer for a metric that is no longer selected is ignored, and the metric list is filled without loading the history several times.
  • All the background requests now run on the IDE's pooled threads instead of raw threads, as recommended by JetBrains.
  • The wording of the paid tier in the interface has been corrected (an ML Experiment Cockpit Pro licence).

2026.1.0 — Pro tier: Compare 2 runs.

  • A fifth tab, Compare: right-click a run in the Experiments tree and choose « Compare with… ». The two runs are shown side by side — parameters, last metric values with absolute and relative gaps — and both metric curves are drawn on the same axis.
  • The whole comparison can be copied as Markdown (both tables) with one click.
  • Pro only: in the Compare view, a run's metric history goes up to 100 000 points per metric (the free chart stays at 5 000 points per metric; the interface then says the series is truncated).
  • Without an ML Experiment Cockpit Pro licence, the Compare tab stays visible but locked, with a « Get Pro » button that opens the JetBrains purchase dialog. The four free tabs — Experiments, Optuna, Models, Sweeps — are unchanged, with the same limits as before (500 experiments, 100 runs per experiment, 500 registered models, 500 model versions, 5 000 metric points per run).

0.0.21 — New description, easier to find.

  • The plugin description on the Marketplace has been rewritten: it now names the four tabs (Experiments, Optuna, Models, Sweeps) and the servers they read, so the plugin shows up in searches that use the words buyers actually type.
  • No functional change; includes the fixes of 0.0.18–0.0.20 below.

0.0.20 — Four display and read defects fixed.

  • Optuna and Models trees now show the readable label of each row (study name, model name, version) instead of the raw Kotlin dump (StudyNode(summary=…)).
  • The Optuna bar chart now picks the hyperparameter that takes the most distinct values, as documented; the numeric tie-breaker is only used when two parameters have the same number of values.
  • A mistyped Optuna URI (for example localhost:8080 without http://) is now reported as Failed to load studies instead of Unexpected error.
  • Optuna trials whose value is inf or -inf (sent as a string by the dashboard) are now read as Infinity and -Infinity; they used to show as “—” and to be left out of the ranking.

0.0.19 — Malformed numbers are reported as invalid JSON.

  • Numbers are now read with the exact JSON grammar (RFC 8259). A response holding a malformed number (for example 1., 1e or 01) is rejected as invalid JSON: the plugin now says that the server did not answer JSON, instead of failing with an opaque conversion error such as For input string: "1.".

0.0.18 — Run tooltips now show.

  • The tooltip of a run in the Experiments tree is now displayed when you hover it: Swing only shows a renderer's tooltip for a component registered with the ToolTipManager, so the run details were silently never shown. This fix was not part of the 0.0.17 build.

0.0.17 — Compatible with the 2026.3 IDE release, and clearer W&B errors.

  • The plugin now declares compatibility up to IDE build 263.*, so it keeps installing on PyCharm 2026.3 instead of becoming obsolete when that release becomes stable.
  • W&B tab: a GraphQL error now shows the server's own message (e.g. "Cannot query field …") instead of a bare "GraphQL error", and an unknown project is reported as "project not found" instead of an empty list.
  • The MLflow and Optuna tabs are unchanged.
